entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Sabiha Rüştü Bozcalı was a visual artist and illustrator who was influential in shaping the visual culture in Turkey in the mid-to-late 20th century. She is considered as "Turkey's first woman illustrator." Bozcalı is known for her portraits, landscapes, still lifes, as well as her illustrations that circulated in advertising, publishing, and through major institutions such as banks and government departments. Her work gained more visibility after she worked as one of the main illustrators of İstanbul Ansiklopedisi, a major encyclopedic work on Istanbul culture, written by historian Reşad Ekrem Koçu.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As 'Turkey's first woman illustrator,' Sabiha Bozcalı contributed significantly to shaping visual culture in Turkey during the mid-to-late 20th century. Her work on İstanbul Ansiklopedisi helped disseminate knowledge of Istanbul culture, leaving a lasting impact on Turkish art and literature.
